scale_006:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up multi-team structure in {{vendor}} (our project-management tool) by creating a team for each department. Approval is required before any changes are applied, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for: (1) the list of departments/teams to create (e.g., Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Support), (2) my organization/workspace name in {{vendor}} if not obvious, and (3) any team-specific settings I want (short key/identifier, description, default workflow states, or initial members) if I have preferences — otherwise use sensible defaults matching {{vendor}}'s standard team setup.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s API (or dashboard if API access isn't available) and confirm you can see the existing workspace structure. For each department I list, prepare a draft team configuration: name, key/identifier, description, and any suggested default settings that would support later cross-team dependency tracking and roadmap views (e.g., consistent naming conventions, shared labels). Do not create or submit anything yet.

Compile a clear summary showing, for each department: the proposed team name, key, description, and settings, plus a note on how this team will connect to others for cross-team dependency tracking later. Present this as a checklist or table.

Report back with this full draft plan and explicitly stop for human sign-off before creating any teams in {{vendor}}. Do not execute the creation calls, submit forms, or make any changes in the workspace — wait for my explicit approval on the draft before proceeding.

scale_006:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure custom workflow states for each team in our {{vendor}} workspace, as part of setting up a multi-team structure. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace/organization URL, (2) the list of teams that need workflow states configured, and (3) for each team, the desired workflow states (e.g. Backlog, Triage, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done, Cancelled) and how they map to underlying status categories (unstarted, started, completed, cancelled). If I don't have per-team specifics ready, propose a sensible default workflow and ask me to confirm or adjust it per team.

Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}}'s workflow/state configuration via its documented public API (or the admin dashboard if the API doesn't expose this), and for each team:
- Draft the exact set of workflow states to add, rename, or remove, matching the naming and category mapping I confirmed.
- Note any dependencies, such as states referenced by existing issues or automation rules that could be affected.
- Prepare a per-team summary showing current states vs. proposed states side by side.

Do NOT apply any changes yet. Compile the full set of proposed workflow-state configurations across all teams into a single clear checklist/diff for my review, and then stop for human sign-off. Once I explicitly approve, you may proceed to create/update/remove the states as specified.

When reporting back, list each team, its current states, proposed states, and any flagged risks (e.g. issues in a state that will be removed). Confirm you have paused and are awaiting my explicit approval before making any changes in {{vendor}}.

scale_006:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up cross-team projects in {{vendor}} (our project-management tool) as part of building a multi-team structure. Approval is required before any changes are actually applied, so your job is to PREPARE everything and then stop for human sign-off — do not create or submit anything live.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: our {{vendor}} workspace/domain, the list of teams involved, the names and goals of the cross-team projects we want to create, the owning team for each project, initial status/priority for each, and any known cross-team dependencies (which teams/projects block or relate to which).

Then, using your configured credentials and {{vendor}}'s documented public API (or its dashboard if the API isn't accessible), research how {{vendor}} models projects, team links, dependencies, and initiatives so your plan matches its actual data model. Draft a clear proposal for each project including: name, description, owning team, linked teams, priority, status, and any cross-team dependency links needed to support the launch coordination. Also note where roadmap/initiative tracking fields would be set (status, priority, owning team) so PMs can track progress later.

Compile this into a single structured summary (e.g., a table or list) showing exactly what would be created or linked in {{vendor}}, with no live API calls or dashboard changes made yet.

When done, report back: the full draft plan for all cross-team projects and dependency links, any {{vendor}} configuration assumptions you made, and any open questions. Then explicitly stop for human sign-off — do not create, submit, or apply any of these projects or links until I approve.

scale_006:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure sprint cycles across multiple teams in our {{vendor}} workspace as part of setting up a multi-team structure. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials, such as: the list of teams that need sprint cycles configured, the desired sprint cadence (e.g., 1-week, 2-week), preferred start day/time for cycles, and whether cadences should be identical across teams or vary per team.

Once you have this information, do the following:
1. For each team, prepare the sprint/cycle configuration using {{vendor}}'s API or admin interface — including cycle length, start date, and naming convention — consistent with the cadence I specify.
2. If {{vendor}} supports auto-generating future cycles on a rolling basis, prepare that setting as part of the configuration.
3. Check for any existing cycles or conflicting settings per team and flag discrepancies before proposing changes.
4. Compile a clear summary/checklist showing, per team: current state, proposed cycle length, start day, and any auto-creation settings — so I can review exactly what will change.

Do not apply, save, or submit any of these configuration changes yet. This step requires a human to explicitly approve the changes before they are applied, so once your checklist and prepared configuration are ready, stop for human sign-off.

When you report back, include: the list of teams covered, the proposed sprint cadence per team, any conflicts or existing cycles you found, and the exact configuration values you intend to submit once I approve. Keep the report concise and organized by team so I can quickly review and give the go-ahead.

scale_006:n5.prompt:
You are helping me set up {{vendor}} channel integrations to support our multi-team Linear/Jira structure (multiple teams, cross-team dependencies, roadmap views, sprint cadences). Please do the following:

1. If you don't already know them, ask me for: (a) the list of teams/squads that need a dedicated {{vendor}} channel, (b) our naming convention preference (e.g., team-<name>), (c) whether channels should be public/open or private, and (d) which Linear/Jira project boards or workflows each channel should relate to for future notifications.

2. Using my configured credentials, prepare the exact set of channel-creation actions needed — one per team — using the CLI command pattern: buzz channels create --name "<team-name>" --type stream --visibility open (adjust visibility per my answer above). Do not execute any creation yet.

3. Draft a summary table listing: proposed channel name, visibility, associated team, and intended purpose (e.g., sprint updates, dependency alerts, roadmap syncs).

4. Check whether an app-directory/marketplace integration exists for connecting {{vendor}} to our issue tracker, and note what it would enable (e.g., posting via incoming webhook, or a bot receiving events via an events API/gateway) — but do not install or authorize anything yet.

5. Present me with the full plan: channel list, naming/visibility choices, and any integration/app-install recommendations, plus the exact CLI commands you intend to run.

Done looks like: a clear, reviewed plan with no channels yet created and no integrations yet installed. Because approval is required before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off once the plan is prepared — do not create channels, install apps, or authorize any integration until I explicitly approve. Report back with the full draft plan and wait for my go-ahead.

You are helping me document our newly configured multi-team project structure (teams, cross-team dependencies, roadmap views, sprint cadences) inside {{vendor}}, our documentation/workspace tool.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} workspace URL or ID, (2) the parent page or space where this doc should live, and (3) any specifics about our team setup (team names, dependency links, roadmap view names, sprint cadence) that you don't already know from prior steps.

Actions to take:
1. Draft a clear, well-structured process document covering: how teams are organized, how cross-team dependencies are tracked and linked, how roadmap views are configured and used, and what the sprint cadence is for each team.
2. Using my configured credentials, create this content as a new page in {{vendor}} via its API (create a new page, e.g. using an operation like POST /v1/pages), nested under the parent page/space I specify.
3. Organize the page with headings/sections matching the four topics above, and include a short summary at the top.
4. Confirm the page was created successfully and share the resulting page link with me.

Because approval is required before changes are applied, do not finalize or publish the page to the team-wide workspace, and do not mark it as an official process doc. Prepare the full draft, the target location, and a checklist of what was included, then stop for human sign-off. I will review the content and location before you make it final or share it broadly.

When reporting back, give me: the draft content or a link to the draft page, the parent location used, and the checklist of sections included, clearly noting that this is pending my approval.
